chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about Zakat al-Fitr.
He عليه السلام said: "If you have set it aside, then it does not harm you whenever you give it, whether before the salat (prayer) or after it."
And he عليه السلام said: "It is obligatory upon you to give on behalf of yourself, your father, your mother, your child, your wife, and your servant."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer), referring here to the Eid prayer
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr, the charity due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.الْوَاجِبُ: that which is obligatory or required
key_terms.خَادِمِكَ: your servant, meaning a dependent under your care
key_terms.عَزَلْتَهَا: you set it aside or separated it for payment
key_terms.وَلَدِكَ: your child, among those included in one's responsibility

ai.seo_question: When must Zakat al-Fitr be given, and for whom is it obligatory to pay it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning Zakat al-Fitr, stating that once it has been set aside, there is no harm in giving it before or after the salat (prayer). It also specifies those for whom a person is responsible to pay it, including oneself and certain family members and dependents.
